prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six opening ballots put B001 first, but unanimity is not the argument. The scientific case is that GLP-1 is a complete arc: proglucagon processing and the incretin effect, identification of the active truncated peptide, receptor-mediated actions on islets, gut and brain, and then therapies whose benefit is confirmed by large independent outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease. The mechanism is settled, the clinical effect is large and durable, and the timing is neither premature nor stale. A prize built on the three physiology and peptide-identification contributions (Holst, Drucker, Mojsov) rewards discovery, which is what the prize has traditionally honoured, and the citation can still name the therapeutic consequence.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is attribution. The three-name cap forces a choice between the discovery arm and the drug-development arm, which excludes Lotte Bjerre Knudsen, whose acylated long-acting analogues are what actually reached patients. Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) form is contested, and early gene-structure and peptide work by others outside the credited list, such as Habener, may be judged equally decisive. A committee that cannot agree on the discovery history may prefer a cleaner candidate even though B001 is the strongest on impact. I take this seriously, but it is a reason to deliberate over names, not to demote the discovery.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranks B001 first but flags whether drug development (Knudsen) should displace a discovery laureate, and puts the SMN2 antisense candidate (B040) fourth as a mechanism-guided therapy.
responses.response: I agree the Knudsen question is the central one, and I come down on the discovery side: the long-acting analogues depend on the physiology and on the identification of the active peptide, and an industrial medicinal-chemistry achievement is harder to credit to one person within a three-person cap. I would give B040 less weight than you do. The SMN2 work is an elegant, rationally designed splicing correction, and I am sympathetic to it as an RNA-processing scientist, but it is one disease and a platform whose generality is still emerging, and the Krainer-Bennett split between mechanism and drug development raises the same discovery-versus-development problem without the breadth of impact that B001 has.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius ranks TNF blockade (B010) second as a mature, clean two-person translational story and argues that recognition is, if anything, overdue.
responses.response: I accept that B010 is mature and cleanly attributed, which is a real advantage over B001. But maturity and clean attribution are not the same as discovery weight. The pivotal advance is a clinical proof that an already-known cytokine is a therapeutic target, and a prize here would sit closer to clinical translation than to the discovery of new biology. You also note the overlap with IL-6 (B002), which suggests the committee would have to justify one cytokine story over another. I would keep B010 as a serious later-year candidate but not ahead of the UPR or CAR-T cases in this round.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks optogenetics (B012) second on originality and lasting methodological impact, and proposes Deisseroth, Hegemann and Nagel despite six credited names.
responses.response: I agree the originality and reproducibility are very high, but I rank it below B051 and B017 because the six-name attribution problem is unusually severe: your trio omits Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck, each with a distinct decisive step, and I do not see a defensible three-person set. I also place weight on the tool-versus-discovery distinction for a Physiology or Medicine prize, since therapeutic relevance is still early. If the committee wants a methods prize, I would want the channelrhodopsin discovery separated from neuronal deployment before I could support a configuration.

responses.point: Svenningsson, as chair, ranks BCR-ABL inhibition (B004) third as the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy and notes that industrial credit within Novartis is diffusely allocated.
responses.response: Imatinib's impact is exceptional, and I did not rank B004 in my opening eight, so I should justify that. My reservation is the one you raise: the credit is a clinical-development and compound-discovery story, and the foundational Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL discoveries sit outside the credited names, which makes a three-person prize on the therapy alone look like an incomplete account. I would reconsider if the committee shows that Druker, Lydon and Sawyers can be framed as a self-contained, defensible achievement.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide is settled enough to include her, and whether Habener or others outside the credited list should displace anyone.
Whether the committee prefers to recognise the physiology and peptide discovery or the drug-development arm, and whether Knudsen should replace a physiology laureate.
How much weight clinical translation should carry relative to mechanistic discovery for B051 (unfolded protein response) and B050 (cGAS-STING), where therapeutic validation is incomplete.
I rely on general knowledge rather than the underlying records for the detailed GLP-1 discovery chronology.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the preferred configuration. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén and share a KI setting, but none of that touches the GLP-1 candidate or the alternatives. My RNA-processing background is adjacent to B040 and B051 (Hac1/XBP1 splicing), but that is shared subject matter, not a personal tie, and I have no documented connection to the named candidates.
